name: Relay: Workspaces & Previews
subtitle: Results, files and handoffs
promotionalText: Inspect workspace output, open supported running apps and follow the source task—all from Relay's Previews tab on iPhone and iPad.
description:
Review the workspace, not just the conversation. Relay connects your iPhone or iPad to a linked computer or Relay Hosted machine so you can inspect the work it produces and decide what comes next. The repository checkout and task execution remain on the connected machine; Relay displays the results you open.

OPEN WORKSPACE RESULTS
The Previews tab brings together files and supported local web results reported by recent jobs. See which workspace and task produced an item, open it and return to its source task. Running-app previews require the app's server to remain running on the linked machine.

START IN THE RIGHT PROJECT
Browse the folders available on your linked machine, inspect files and start a task in the right workspace. Work stays associated with its project, conversation and run history.

PICK UP A HANDOFF
Use the companion Relay CLI to hand off supported coding sessions from your Mac. On the phone, review the source repository, computer, changes and conversation excerpt before continuing the task. Handoffs use your GitHub repository and a configured Relay machine. Continuation capabilities depend on the provider and session format.

KEEP DECISIONS WITH YOU
Follow sessions across workspaces. Review supported agent approval requests, see the requested action, and approve or deny it from the phone. Provider capabilities depend on the connected machine and configuration.

CHOOSE WHERE WORK RUNS
Connect hardware you manage, or use a Relay-hosted machine. Relay Hosted is offered through monthly or yearly auto-renewing in-app subscriptions. Both plans provide the same hosted-machine service. AI provider access is separate and is not included in a Relay Hosted subscription.

CONTROL AI DATA SHARING
Before sending work to a selected AI provider, Relay identifies the recipient and requests permission. Work content may include your prompt, conversation history, workspace files, attachments and command output, including personal data contained in that content. You can review the disclosure even while the provider is disconnected.

Relay requires a Relay account. Agent runs require a compatible connected machine and authentication with the selected provider. Supported providers include Codex, Claude Code, Cursor and Kimi, subject to availability on that machine. Work executes on the connected machine, not on iOS.

Subscriptions renew automatically unless canceled at least 24 hours before the current period ends. Payment is charged to your Apple ID. Manage or cancel subscriptions in your App Store account settings.

reviewNotesDraft:
Use the existing Sign-in Information fields for the review account. No additional credentials are included in these notes. Preserve the existing account, hosted-machine and sandbox-purchase instructions.

RELAY WORKSPACE-TO-RESULT WORKFLOW
The attached replacement build adds a first-class Previews tab. Workspace results is the primary source and uses the current linked machine. Published catalog is a separate, configured source with its own access requirements; the review account does not need that catalog to review workspace results.

1. Open Previews > Workspace results. The prepared review task shows its real generated files and supported running-app output, with the workspace and source task identified.
2. Open the prepared artifact to inspect the generated result. For the task's running-app result, use Open live app. The preview is created from a localhost URL returned by that task. Its server remains on the linked machine; the phone does not connect to its own localhost. Use View source job to inspect the run that produced the result.
3. Open Workspaces and select the prepared review workspace. Browse its files, then open a conversation in that folder. Work is scoped to the configured project rather than an arbitrary phone-supplied filesystem path.
4. Open Threads in the conversation. A prepared handoff, when available, shows its source repository, computer, change summary and excerpt. Continue picks up the supported handoff on the Relay machine. A Mac session listed without a handoff offers a new session instead of claiming exact continuation.
5. Open Sessions to inspect recent work. If a supported agent run is waiting for approval, its request shows the action and provides Approve, Deny and Open. Approval availability depends on the provider and run.
6. Settings shows the linked computer and, for a hosted account, Relay Hosted subscription controls and Restore Purchases. A Relay Hosted subscription does not include an AI provider subscription.

AI DATA SHARING
The provider-specific disclosure appears before the provider is ready to send. It is always reopenable using AI data sharing above the composer, including when the screen says Needs Connection. It names the recipient and lists the prompt, conversation history, workspace files, attachments and command output, including personal data within that work content. Not Now sends nothing. Allow records consent but does not send a prompt; a separate Send action is required. Relay does not send its account name/email, password, device identifiers or Apple payment/subscription details to the AI provider as account metadata.

reviewReplyDraft:
Hello App Review,

Thank you for the feedback under Guideline 4.3(a). The replacement build adds a first-class Previews tab that makes Relay's workspace-to-result workflow directly accessible. The updated listing and screenshots show this actual workflow.

Workspace results brings together files and supported running-app output reported by recent jobs on the currently linked machine. Each result retains its workspace and source-task context. A running-app preview is created from a localhost URL returned by that specific task, with expiring task-linked access, so the result can be inspected inside Relay. Published catalog is a separate, configured source; catalog metadata is verified by its signature, and each entry explains any certificate requirement. The primary workspace-results flow does not require catalog access.

Relay's native SwiftUI client works with the companion Relay CLI and Relay machine service. The implementation also includes workspace-scoped runs and file inspection, supported Mac-to-machine handoff with source context and a Continue action, and an approval-request inbox with the requested action and explicit decisions. Conversation handoff data is sealed to the receiving machine; the repository checkout and task execution remain on that machine. Provider/session capabilities are stated in the app rather than represented as universal continuation support.

These behaviors are implemented across the native client and companion services. Repository history records the prototype-manifest client in May, handoff integration in August, and task-linked preview implementation in August. We can provide further implementation details if useful. We have retained provider-specific AI data-sharing permission and the choice of user-managed hardware or Relay Hosted.

The updated App Review Information gives the verified workspace and task names and steps for inspecting the prepared results. The existing review account and sandbox-purchase access remain available.

Your message did not identify a specific matching app, binary component or screen. If a similarity concern remains, could you identify the particular functionality or material you consider duplicated, or provide any comparison details you can share? That will help us address the concern precisely.

Thank you.
